ESB was established in 1927 as a statutory corporation in the Republic of Ireland under the Electricity (Supply) Act 1927. With a holding of approximately 97.1%, ESB is majority owned by the Irish Government. The remaining approximate 2.9% is held by the trustees of an Employee Share Ownership Plan. As a strong, diversified, vertically integrated utility, ESB operates right across the electricity market: from generation, through transmission and distribution, to supply. In addition, ESB extracts further value at certain points along this chain: supplying gas, using our networks to carry fibre for telecommunications, developing electric vehicle public charging infrastructure and more. ESB is a leading Irish utility focused on providing excellent customer service and maintaining our financial strength. We have a regulated asset base of approximately €12 billion with 30% of electricity generation capacity in the all-island market.

It also provides historical data that is very important for recognising trends and proactively addressing issues. This will not be restricted to ControlUp related products as other digital monitoring solutions will be considered. SCOPE OF SERVICE The Contractor shall provide enterprise -grade mobile and data services to the U.S. Embassy Panama. The prices listed below shall include all labor, service, equipment, technical support, materials, insurance (see FAR 52.228 -4 and 52.228- 5), overhead, and profit. The Government will pay the Contractor on a monthly basis for routine services that have been satisfactorily performed. The Contractor shall ensure that all services are delivered with high availability, reliability, and performance consistent with commercial best practices for enterprise telecommunications services. The Contractor shall offer two different plans to fulfill the Government needs: Basic Plan. Pay per use for actual calls (local, local long distance, international long distance), incoming and outgoing roaming calls, incoming and outgoing local SMS, incoming and outgoing international SMS, incoming and outgoing roaming SMS. Unlimited Smart Phones & Tablets Plan. A flat monthly rate per cellphone line that includes unlimited: local data, local minutes on-net, local minutes off-net, national long-distance minutes,

International calling services shall support clear and reliable voice communications consistent with the best commercial practices for enterprise telecommunications services. INTERNATIONAL ROAMING The Contractor shall provide broad international roaming coverage for voice, SMS, and data services through commercially established roaming agreements with foreign mobile network operators. Emphasis shall be placed on roaming availability and service reliability throughout the Western Hemisphere. The Contractor shall support international roaming services compatible with 4G/LTE services, and/or 5G services (5G services where commercially available). The Contractor shall provide the COR with an updated list of current international roaming partners and supported roaming countries at least every six (6) months. The Contractor shall disclose any significant roaming restrictions, unsupported regions, or service limitations in its proposal. SMS MESSAGING The Contractor shall provide reliable SMS messaging services on a 24- hour basis, including domestic, inter

ns and changes, lost or stolen device r eporting, billing inquiries, and service troubleshooting. The Contractor shall provide dedicated account management and support personnel who are fluent in both English and Spanish. The Contractor shall provide a dedicated customer support email address for the U.S. Embassy Panama. This capability must allow operators to identify and prioritize interoperability issues and potential workarounds within a single system. • 3.1.3.2 Platform Issue Tracking: The software shall provide a mechanism to record and maintain a history of platform-specific issues (e.g., design, testing, operational) through their entire lifecycle. This information must be linked to the platform specification to enable automatic updates to existing analyses. • 3.1.3.3 Capabilities & Limitations Summary: The software shall be capable of generating a consolidated, high-level summary of a platform's TDL capabilities, including implemented TDLs, message baselines, equipment fits, and network capabilities (e.g., Link 22, JREAP). 3.1.4 Interoperability (IO) Evaluation: The software shall provide a robust module to conduct detailed, multi-platform IO evaluations.
